terms.gloss: punctuation, the marking of divisions between words
terms.comment: The verb is interpungere, to punctuate: cum scrībimus, interpungere cōnsuēvimus, when we write we are used to punctuating (Sen. Ep. 40, Lewis & Short). A punctuation mark is interpūnctum (Cic. de Or. 3.181; Traupman 248). Ancient Latin marked word divisions with points; the modern marks have modern names (see comma, full stop, question mark).

terms.gloss: a punctuation mark, a division made by a point
evidence: Cic. de Or. 3.181: interpūncta verbōrum (Lewis & Short)

phrases.english: when we write, we are used to punctuating

sources: Lewis & Short: interpunctio · Lewis & Short: interpunctum · Lewis & Short: interpungo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 248.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
